title: Nine Bricks and One Dry Hour
subtitle: 户外烧烤 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 户外烧烤（生活与学习·饮食与烹饪）
meta: 主题语境：户外烧烤（生活与学习·饮食与烹饪）　|　核心词汇：barbecue　|　正文 339 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 barbecue 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1966 my father built ① a barbecue out of nine bricks and was proud of it for eleven years, and my mother said the building was the whole of the event. The ② barbecue, meaning the thing in the garden and not the cooking, rusted by the second summer and was never moved; a barbecue, he said, is the only piece of furniture that is judged by its worst afternoon.

Every ③ barbecue in that road was cancelled by the weather, and the ④ barbecue in June, meaning the one that actually happened and not either of those, is remembered as though it had been sunny. A barbecue, my grandmother said, is nine parts optimism and one part a dry hour; my father said the optimism is the part you build with bricks.

My aunt meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ barbecue was the whole of the smoke, meaning the smell in the hedge and not the bricks. The ⑥ barbecue, meaning the smell and not any of that, is the only thing in a garden that the neighbours share whether they were asked or not; a barbecue, she said, is either a thing you cook on or the only invitation you cannot refuse. He said the smoke was never invited.

By 1979 the ⑦ barbecue had become a photograph of a wet afternoon, and the photograph had become an argument about whether it had ever been summer. The ⑧ barbecue of the whole thing, my father wrote in August, was nine years of rust and one dry hour; a barbecue, he said, is either the bricks in the garden or the reason the neighbours know your name. She said the knowing was the part that lasted.

The ⑨ barbecue I remember is the one in June, which everybody describes as sunny and which was not. A ⑩ barbecue, my mother said in 1981, is the only meal that improves by being rained on; every barbecue, she said, is an optimism that has agreed to look like a garden. He said the garden was the alibi.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 烤肉架（指花园里那个东西，与烹饪相对）
C. 固定搭配：build a barbecue 砌一个烤肉架
D. n. 烧烤；户外烧烤（指那条路上每一次）
E. n. 烧烤（指六月那一次）
F. n. 烧烤（指那阵烟、气味）
G. n. 烧烤（抽象：那股味道这件事）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: a barbecue out of nine bricks
The barbecue, meaning the thing in the garden and not the cooking
barbecue was the whole of the smoke
the barbecue had become a photograph of a wet afternoon
The barbecue of the whole thing
A barbecue, my mother said in 1981

answers.why: build a barbecue 意为“砌一个烤肉架”，1966 年父亲用九块砖砌了一个烤肉架，并为它骄傲了十一年。
barbecue 意为“烤肉架”，指花园里那个东西而不是烹饪，它第二个夏天就锈了，从此再没挪过。
barbecue 指那条路上每一次烧烤，那条路上每一次烧烤都被天气取消了。
barbecue 指六月那一次（真正办成的那一次），它被记得好像那天是晴天一样。
barbecue 意为“烧烤”，指那阵烟、那股气味，姑姑说它是烟的全部，指的是树篱里的味道。
barbecue 为抽象用法，指那股味道这件事，是花园里唯一邻居不问自得的东西。
barbecue 意为“烤肉架”，到 1979 年这个 barbecue 成了一个潮湿下午的一张照片。
barbecue 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，父亲八月写道，整件事权衡下来是九年的铁锈和一个干燥的钟头。
barbecue 意为“烧烤”，我记得的是六月那一次，人人都说那天晴，其实不是。
barbecue 为抽象总称，母亲说烧烤是唯一会因为被雨淋而变得更好的一顿饭。
